feedback: D1: This is a genuinely strong catalogue. You quoted the login concatenation for SQL injection (A03/CWE-89), the MD5 hashing line, the alg:none skip branch, the missing exp/nbf for no token expiry (CWE-613), the open redirect on next, the setcookie without Secure (CWE-614), the XXE ENTITY file:///etc/passwd line, and the files/?path=/etc/passwd traversal. Nine of the ten real findings are present with evidence, which is well above a partial catalogue. Two real problems hold the row back. The hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 should be its own finding as A05/CWE-798, not folded into a vague weak-and-guessable note, and you missed the stored-XSS cookie beacon at 02:18:47 to 185.220.101.9:8443 that proves exfiltration. The decoy is also inverted. The safe construct is the HS256 verify branch that uses hash_equals, which is constant-time and sound, so the right move is to name it, show it is safe at the mechanism level, and explain that the real bugs are alg:none and the hardcoded secret. You instead labeled JWT-HS256-is-secure as FALSE and called it insecure, which disproves the safe construct rather than proving it safe, so that part earns nothing. D2: The chain is mostly in the right order and several hops carry verbatim PoCs (admin' OR '1'='1, the next redirect, the path traversal, the XXE entity), but the stored-XSS hop has no payload, the SQLi CVSS uses A:H when the bypass does not touch availability so it should be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at roughly 9.1, and the impact is bare. You wrote 312 customers but gave no naira, no balances up to about 950k summing to tens of millions, no BoltCash tie-in, and no stated assumptions, which is most of the impact row. D3: The executive summary ends on a generic call to action rather than the customers-and-naira headline a board needs, only five findings carry evidence here, the decoy is restated incorrectly, no earliest-break fix is named, the detection stopgaps give patterns and a Low false-positive note but no exact log field, and the remediation is explicitly ordered by CVSS severity rather than by effort-to-risk, which caps that row at half. D4: You answer all four prompts in your own voice, cite ISC2 Canon II by number in a load-bearing way, and anchor to the 312 records, but you name the NDPA only in general and never cite section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification or section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects, so that row is empty. I have to be straight with you about the most serious issue. The SSRF to 169.254.169.254 metadata with IAM credentials and full infrastructure compromise does not exist in this pack, there is no capture line for it, and it drove your headline CVSS 9.9. Inventing an exploit and evidence is fabrication, so that finding scores zero and a five-point penalty applies. I looked hard for a way to round this up because your real catalogue is strong, but the fabricated SSRF, the inverted decoy, and the missing impact figures will not support a higher mark. The single most important fix is to stop inventing findings: grade only what the evidence proves, get the decoy right by proving the hash_equals branch safe, and quantify impact in naira tied to the 312 BoltCash customers.
